verses.en: The trees, the moon, and the wolf will soon speak openly of your prophethood.

verses.ar: وَمَركَبُكَ الْبُراقُ إِلى جَمَالِكَ مُشتَاقٌ
verses.tr: Wa markabukal-burāqu ilā jamālika mushtāq
verses.en: Your mount, al-Buraq, longs for your beauty.

verses.ar: وَجِبرِيلُ شَاوُوشُ مَملَكَتِكَ قَدْ أَعلَنَ بِذِكرِكَ فِي الْآفَاقِ
verses.tr: Wa Jibrīlu shāwūshu mamlakatika qad aʿlana bi-dhikrika fil-āfāq
verses.en: And Jibril, the herald of your kingdom, has already proclaimed your remembrance across the horizons.

verses.ar: وَالقَمَرُ مَأمُورٌ لَكَ بِالانشِقَاقْ
verses.tr: Wal-qamaru maʾmūrun laka bil-inshiqāq
verses.en: And the moon has been commanded to split for you.

verses.ar: وَقِيلَ لِبَعضِهِمْ: كَأَنَّ وَجهَهُ الْقَمَرْ، فَقَالَ: بَلْ أَضْوَأُ مِنَ الْقَمَرِ، إِذَا لَمْ يَحُلْ دُونَهُ الْغَمَامُ، قَدْ غَشِيَهُ الْجَلالُ وَانْتَهَىْ إلْيهِ الْكَمَالُ
verses.tr: Wa qīla li-baʿḍihim: ka-anna wajhahul-qamar, fa-qāla: bal aḍwaʾu minal-qamari, idhā lam yaḥul dūnahul-ghamām, qad ghashiyahul-jalālu wantahā ilayhil-kamāl
verses.en: It was said to some of them: His face was like the moon. He replied: Rather brighter than the moon when no cloud veils it — majesty enveloped him, and perfection reached its fullness in him.

verses.ar: وَبَينَمَا الْحَبِيبُ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ عَلَيهِ وَسَلَّمَ مُنصِتٌ لِسَمَاعِ تِلكَ الْأَشبَاحِ، وَوَجهُهُ مُتَهَلِّلٌ كَنُورِ الصَّبَاحِ
verses.tr: Wa baynamal-ḥabību ﷺ munṣitun li-samāʿi tilkal-ashbāḥ, wa wajhuhu mutahallilun ka-nūriṣ-ṣabāḥ
verses.en: And while the Beloved ﷺ was quietly listening to those forms, his face beaming like the light of morning,

verses.ar: إِذْ أَقبَلَتْ حَلِيمَةُ مُعلِنَةً بِالصِّيَاحِ تَقُولُ: وَاغَرِيبَاهُ. فَقَالَتِ الْمَلائِكَةُ: مَا أَنتَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ بِغَرِيبٍ، بَلْ أَنْتَ مِنَ اللّٰهِ قَرِيبٌ، وَأَنتَ لَهُ صَفِيٌّ وَحَبِيبٌ
verses.tr: Idh aqbalat Ḥalīmatu muʿlinatan biṣ-ṣiyāḥi taqūlu: wā gharībāh. Fa-qālatil-malāʾikatu: mā anta yā Muḥammadu bi-gharīb, bal anta mina-Llāhi qarīb, wa anta lahu ṣafiyyun wa ḥabīb
verses.en: Halima came crying out: 'O my poor lonely one!' The angels said: 'You are no stranger, O Muhammad; rather you are near to Allah, His chosen one and His beloved.'

verses.ar: قَالَتْ حَلِيمَةُ: وَاوَحِيدَاهُ. فَقَالَتِ الْمَلائِكَةُ: يَا مُحَمَّدُ، مَا أَنتَ بِوَحِيد، بَلْ أَنتَ صَاحِبُ التَّأيِيدِ، وَأَنِيسُكَ الْحَمِيدُ الْمَجِيدُ، وَإِخوَانُكَ الْمَلائِكَةُ وَأَهلُ التَّوحِيدِ
verses.tr: Qālat Ḥalīmatu: wā waḥīdāh. Fa-qālatil-malāʾikatu: yā Muḥammadu, mā anta bi-waḥīd, bal anta ṣāḥibut-taʾyīd, wa anīsukal-ḥamīdul-majīd, wa ikhwānukal-malāʾikatu wa ahlut-tawḥīd
verses.en: Halima said: 'O my lonely one!' The angels said: 'O Muhammad, you are not alone; you are the one granted divine support; your companion is the Praiseworthy, the Glorious; and your brethren are the angels and the people of divine oneness.'

verses.ar: قَالَتْ حَلِيمَةُ: وَايَتِيمَاهُ. فَقَالَتِ الْمَلائِكَةُ: لِلّٰهِ دَرُّكَ مِن يَتِيمٍ، فَإِنَّ قَدرَكَ عِندَ اللّٰهِ عَظِيم
verses.tr: Qālat Ḥalīmatu: wā yatīmāh. Fa-qālatil-malāʾikatu: lillāhi darruka min yatīmin, fa-inna qadraka ʿinda-Llāhi ʿaẓīm
verses.en: Halima said: 'O my orphan!' The angels said: 'How excellent an orphan you are! For your rank with Allah is tremendous.'

verses.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَلِيمَةُ سَالِمًا مِنَ الْأَهوَالِ رَجَعَتْ بِهِ مَسرُورَةً إِلَى الْأَطلالِ، ثُمَّ قَصَّتْ خَبَرَهُ عَلٰى بَعضِ الْكُهَّانْ
verses.tr: Falammā raʾat-hu Ḥalīmatu sāliman minal-ahwāli rajaʿat bihi masrūratan ilal-aṭlāl, thumma qaṣṣat khabarahu ʿalā baʿḍil-kuhhān
verses.en: When Halima saw him safe from all terrors, she returned with him joyfully to her camp, then related his story to some of the soothsayers.

verses.ar: وَأَعَادَتْ عَلَيهِ مَا تَمَّ مِنْ أَمرِهِ وَمَا كَانَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ الْكَاهِنُ: يَا ابْنَ زَمزَمَ وَالْمَقَامِ وَالرُّكنِ وَالبَيتِ الْحَرَامِ، أَفِيْ الْيَقْظَةِ رَأَيْتَ هٰذَا أَمْ فِيْ الْمَنَامِ؟
verses.tr: Wa aʿādat ʿalayhi mā tamma min amrihi wa mā kān, fa-qāla lahul-kāhinu: yā-bna Zamzama wal-Maqāmi war-Rukni wal-Baytil-ḥarām, a-fil-yaqẓati raʾayta hādhā am fil-manām?
verses.en: She recounted to him all that had happened, and the soothsayer said to him: 'O son of Zamzam, the Station, the Corner, and the Sacred House — did you see this while awake or in a dream?'

verses.ar: فَقَالَ وَحُرْمَةِ الْمَلِكِ الْعَلَّامِ، شَاهَدتُهُمْ كِفَاحًا لا أَشُكُّ فِيْ ذٰلِكَ وَلا أُضَامُ
verses.tr: Fa-qāla wa ḥurmatil-malikil-ʿallām, shāhadtuhum kifāḥan lā ashukku fī dhālika wa lā uḍām
verses.en: He said: 'By the sanctity of the All-Knowing King, I saw them face to face; I have no doubt of it, nor am I deceived.'

verses.ar: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْكَاهِنُ: أَبشِرْ أَيُّهَا الْغُلامُ، فَأَنتَ صَاحِبُ الْأَعلامِ، وَنُبُوَّتُكَ لِلأَنبِيَاءِ قِفلٌ وَخِتَامٌ، وَعَلَيكَ يَنزِلُ جِبرِيلُ، وَعَلى بِسَاطِ الْقُدسِ يُخَاطِبُكَ الْجَلِيلُ
verses.tr: Fa-qāla lahul-kāhinu: abshir ayyuhal-ghulām, fa-anta ṣāḥibul-aʿlām, wa nubuwwatuka lil-anbiyāʾi qiflun wa khitām, wa ʿalayka yanzilu Jibrīl, wa ʿalā bisāṭil-qudsi yukhāṭibukal-jalīl
verses.en: The soothsayer said: 'Rejoice, O boy! You are the bearer of the banners; your prophethood is the lock and seal upon all prophethood; upon you Jibril will descend, and upon the carpet of holiness the Majestic One will address you.'

verses.ar: وَمَنْ ذَا الذِّيْ يَحصُرُ مَا حَوَيتَ مِنَ التَّفضِيلِ، وَعَنْ بَعضِ وَصفِ مَعنَاكَ يَقصُرُ لِسَانُ الْمَادِحِ الْمُطِيلِ
verses.tr: Wa man dhal-ladhī yaḥṣuru mā ḥawayta minat-tafḍīl, wa ʿan baʿḍi waṣfi maʿnāka yaqṣuru lisānul-mādiḥil-muṭīl
verses.en: Who could ever encompass the excellences you contain? Even the tongue of the most lavish praiser falls short of describing a fraction of your reality.

verses.ar: وَكَانَ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ عَلَيهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَحسَنَ النَّاسِ خَلقًا وَخُلُقًا، وَأَهْدَاهُمْ إِلَىْ الْحَقِّ طُرُقًا، وَكَانَ خُلُقُهُ الْقُرْآنَ
verses.tr: Wa kāna ﷺ aḥsanan-nāsi khalqan wa khuluqan, wa ahdāhum ilal-ḥaqqi ṭuruqan, wa kāna khuluquhul-Qurʾān
verses.en: He ﷺ was the finest of people in form and in character, the most rightly guiding of them to the truth — and his character was the Qur'an itself.

verses.ar: وَشِيمَتُهُ الْغُفرَانَ، يَنصَحُ لِلإِنسَانِ، وَيَفسَحُ فِيْ الْإِحسَانِ، وَيَعفُو عَنِ الذَّنبِ إِنْ كَانَ فِيْ حَقِّهِ وَسَبَبِهْ
verses.tr: Wa shīmatuhul-ghufrān, yanṣaḥu lil-insān, wa yafsaḥu fil-iḥsān, wa yaʿfū ʿanidh-dhanbi in kāna fī ḥaqqihi wa sababih
verses.en: Forgiveness was his nature; he gave sincere counsel to people, was expansive in doing good, and pardoned wrongs done against him.

verses.ar: فَإِذَا ضُيِّعَ حَقُّ اللّٰهِ لَمْ يَقُمْ أَحَدٌ لِغَضَبِهِ، مَنْ رَآهُ بَدِيهَةً هَابَهُ، وَإِذَا دَعَاهُ الْمِسكِينُ أَجَابَهُ
verses.tr: Fa-idhā ḍuyyiʿa ḥaqqu-Llāhi lam yaqum aḥadun li-ghaḍabihi, man raʾāhu badīhatan hābahu, wa idhā daʿāhul-miskīnu ajābah
verses.en: But when a right of Allah was violated, none could stand before his anger. Whoever saw him unexpectedly was struck with awe of him, and when a poor person called upon him, he answered.

verses.ar: يَقُولُ الْحَقَّ وَلَوْ كَانَ مُرًّا، وَلاَ يُضْمِرُ لِمُسلِمٍ غِشًّا وَلا ضُرًّا
verses.tr: Yaqūlul-ḥaqqa wa law kāna murran, wa lā yuḍmiru li-muslimin ghishshan wa lā ḍurrā
verses.en: He spoke the truth even if it was bitter, and he harboured toward no Muslim any deceit or harm.

verses.ar: مَنْ نَظَرَ فِيْ وَجْهِهِ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ لَيسَ بِوَجْهِ كَذَّابٍ، وَكَانَ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ عَلَيهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَيسَ بِغَمَّازٍ وَلا عَيَّابٍ
verses.tr: Man naẓara fī wajhihi ʿalima annahu laysa bi-wajhi kadhdhāb, wa kāna ﷺ laysa bi-ghammāzin wa lā ʿayyāb
verses.en: Whoever looked into his face knew it was not the face of a liar; and he ﷺ was neither a backbiter nor a faultfinder.

verses.ar: إِذَا سُرَّ كَأَنَّ وَجهَهُ قِطعَةُ قَمَرٍ، وَإِذَا كَلَّمَ النَّاسَ، فَكَأَنَّمَا يَجنُونَ مِنْ كَلامِهِ أَحلَىْ ثَمَرٍ
verses.tr: Idhā surra ka-anna wajhahu qiṭʿatu qamar, wa idhā kallaman-nāsa, fa-ka-annamā yajnūna min kalāmihi aḥlā thamar
verses.en: When he was glad, his face was like a piece of the moon; and when he spoke to people, it was as though they were gathering the sweetest fruit from his words.

verses.ar: وَإِذَا تَبَسَّمَ تَبَسَّمَ عَنْ مِثلِ حَبِّ الْغَمَامِ، وَإِذَا تَكَلَّمَ فَكَأَنَّ الدُّرَّ يَسقُطُ مِن ذٰلِكَ الْكَلامِ، وَإِذَا تَحَدَّثَ فَكَأَنَّ الْمِسكَ يَخرُجُ مِن فِيهِ
verses.tr: Wa idhā tabassama tabassama ʿan mithli ḥabbil-ghamām, wa idhā takallama fa-ka-annad-durra yasquṭu min dhālikal-kalām, wa idhā taḥaddatha fa-ka-annal-miska yakhruju min fīh
verses.en: When he smiled, his teeth shone like hailstones of a cloud; when he spoke, it was as though pearls fell from his words; and when he conversed, it was as though musk issued from his mouth.

verses.ar: وَإِذَا مَرَّ بِطَرِيقٍ عُرِفَ مِنْ طِيبِهِ أَنَّهُ قَد مَرَّ فِيهِ
verses.tr: Wa idhā marra bi-ṭarīqin ʿurifa min ṭībihi annahu qad marra fīh
verses.en: When he passed along a road, it was known from his fragrance that he had passed there.

verses.ar: وَإِذَا جَلَسَ فِيْ مَجلِسٍ بَقِيَ طِيبُهُ فِيهِ أَيَّامًا وَإِنْ تَغَيَّبَ، وَيُوجَدُ مِنْهُ أَحسَنُ طِيبٍ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ قَدْ تَطَيَّبَ
verses.tr: Wa idhā jalasa fī majlisin baqiya ṭībuhu fīhi ayyāman wa in taghayyab, wa yūjadu minhu aḥsanu ṭībin, wa in lam yakun qad taṭayyab
verses.en: When he sat in a gathering, his fragrance lingered there for days after he had left; and the finest scent came from him, though he had used no perfume.

verses.ar: وَإِذَا مَشَىْ بَينَ أَصحَابِهِ فَكَأَنَّهُ الْقَمَرُ بَينَ النُّجُومِ الزُّهَرِ
verses.tr: Wa idhā mashā bayna aṣḥābihi fa-ka-annahul-qamaru baynan-nujūmiz-zuhar
verses.en: When he walked among his companions, he was like the moon among the bright shining stars.

verses.ar: وَإِذَا أَقبَلَ لَيْلاً فَكَأَنَّ النَّاسَ مِنْ نُورِهِ فِيْ أَوَانِ الظُّهرِ
verses.tr: Wa idhā aqbala laylan fa-ka-annan-nāsa min nūrihi fī awāniẓ-ẓuhr
verses.en: When he approached by night, his light made people feel as though it were the hour of noon.

verses.ar: وَكَانَ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ عَلَيهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَجوَدَ بِالخَيرِ مِنَ الرِّيحِ الْمُرسَلَةِ، وَكَانَ يُرفَقُ بِاليَتِيمِ وَالأَرمَلَةِ
verses.tr: Wa kāna ﷺ ajwada bil-khayri minar-rīḥil-mursalati, wa kāna yarfuqu bil-yatīmi wal-armalah
verses.en: He ﷺ was more generous with good than the sent wind, and he was gentle with the orphan and the widow.

verses.ar: وَقَالَ بَعضُ وَاصِفِيهِ: مَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْ ذِيْ لُمَّةٍ سَودَاءَ فِيْ حُلَّةٍ حَمرَاءَ، أَحسَنَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللّٰهِ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ عَلَيهِ وَسَلَّمَ
verses.tr: Wa qāla baʿḍu wāṣifīhi: mā raʾaytu min dhī lummatin sawdāʾa fī ḥullatin ḥamrāʾa, aḥsana min rasūli-Llāhi ﷺ
verses.en: One who described him said: 'I never saw anyone with black locks in a red garment more beautiful than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'

verses.ar: وَقِيلَ لِبَعضِهِمْ: كَأَنَّ وَجهَهُ الْقَمَرْ، فَقَالَ: بَلْ أَضْوَأُ مِنَ الْقَمَرِ، إِذَا لَمْ يَحُلْ دُونَهُ الْغَمَامُ، قَدْ غَشِيَهُ الْجَلالُ وَانْتَهَىْ إِلَيهِ الْكَمَالُ
verses.tr: Wa qīla li-baʿḍihim: ka-anna wajhahul-qamar, fa-qāla: bal aḍwaʾu minal-qamari, idhā lam yaḥul dūnahul-ghamām, qad ghashiyahul-jalālu wantahā ilayhil-kamāl
verses.en: It was said to some of them: His face was like the moon. He replied: Rather brighter than the moon when no cloud veils it; majesty enveloped him, and perfection reached its fullness in him.

verses.ar: قَالَ بَعضُ وَاصِفِيهِ: مَا رَأَيْتُ قَبْلَهُ وَلاَ بَعدَهُ مِثلَهُ
verses.tr: Qāla baʿḍu wāṣifīhi: mā raʾaytu qablahu wa lā baʿdahu mithlah
verses.en: One who described him said: 'I never saw, before him or after him, anyone like him.'

verses.ar: فَيَعجَزُ لِسَانُ الْبَلِيغِ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يُحصِيَ فَضلَهُ
verses.tr: Fa-yaʿjazu lisānul-balīghi idhā arāda an yuḥṣiya faḍlah
verses.en: The tongue of the most eloquent fails when it tries to enumerate his excellence.

verses.ar: فَسُبْحَانَ مَنْ خَصَّهُ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ عَلَيهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِالْمَحَلِّ الْأَسْنَىْ، وَأَسْرَىْ بِهِ إِلَى قَابِ قَوسَينِ أَوْ أَدْنَىْ
verses.tr: Fa-subḥāna man khaṣṣahu ﷺ bil-maḥallil-asnā, wa asrā bihi ilā qābi qawsayni aw adnā
verses.en: Glory be to the One who singled him ﷺ out with the loftiest station, and took him by night to the distance of two bows' length or nearer.

verses.ar: وَأَيَّدَهُ بِالْمُعْجِزَاتِ الَّتِيْ لاَ تُحْصَىْ
verses.tr: Wa ayyadahu bil-muʿjizātil-latī lā tuḥṣā
verses.en: And supported him with miracles beyond counting,

verses.ar: وَأَوْفَاهُ مِنْ خِصَالِ الْكَمَالِ مَا يَجِلُّ أَنْ يُستَقصَىْ، وَأَعْطَاهُ خَمْسَةً لَمْ يُعْطِهِنَّ أَحَدًا قَبلَهُ
verses.tr: Wa awfāhu min khiṣālil-kamāli mā yajillu an yustaqṣā, wa aʿṭāhu khamsatan lam yuʿṭihinna aḥadan qablah
verses.en: and granted him such perfect qualities as are too great to be fully counted, and gave him five things He had given to none before him.

verses.ar: وَآتَاهُ جَوَامِعَ الْكَلِمِ، فَلَمْ يُدرِكْ أَحَدٌ فَضْلَهُ
verses.tr: Wa ātāhu jawāmiʿal-kalim, fa-lam yudrik aḥadun faḍlah
verses.en: He gave him the most comprehensive of speech; no one has grasped the full measure of his merit.

verses.ar: وَكَانَ لَهُ فِيْ كُلِّ مَقَامٍ مَقَالٌ، وَلِكُلِّ كَمَالٍ مِنهُ كَمَالٌ
verses.tr: Wa kāna lahu fī kulli maqāmin maqāl, wa li-kulli kamālin minhu kamāl
verses.en: In every station he had the fitting word, and to every perfection he added a perfection of his own.

verses.ar: لاَ يَحُورُ فِيْ سُؤَالٍ وَلاَ جَوَابٍ، وَلاَ يَجُولُ لِسَانُهُ إِلْاَّ فِيْ صَوَابٍ
verses.tr: Lā yaḥūru fī suʾālin wa lā jawāb, wa lā yajūlu lisānuhu illā fī ṣawāb
verses.en: He was never at a loss in question or answer, and his tongue moved in nothing but what was correct.

verses.ar: وَمَا عَسَىْ أَنْ يُقَالَ فِيْ مَنْ وَصَفَهُ الْقُرْآنْ، وَأَعْرَبَ عَنْ فَضَائِلِهِ التَّورَاةُ وَالإِنجِيلُ وَالزَّبُورُ وَالفُرقَانْ
verses.tr: Wa mā ʿasā an yuqāla fī man waṣafahul-Qurʾān, wa aʿraba ʿan faḍāʾilihit-Tawrātu wal-Injīlu waz-Zabūru wal-Furqān
verses.en: And what more can be said of one whom the Qur'an described, and whose excellences the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion all made known?

verses.ar: وَجَمَعَ اللّٰهُ لَهُ بَينَ رُؤْيَتِهِ وَكَلامِهِ، وَقَرَنَ اسْمَهُ مَعَ اسْمِهِ تَنبِيهًا عَلٰى عُلُوِّ مَقَامِهِ
verses.tr: Wa jamaʿa-Llāhu lahu bayna ruʾyatihi wa kalāmihi, wa qarana-smahu maʿa-smihi tanbīhan ʿalā ʿuluwwi maqāmih
verses.en: Allah joined for him both the seeing of Him and the speaking with Him, and coupled his name with His own Name, as a sign of the loftiness of his station.

verses.ar: وَجَعَلَهُ رَحمَةً لِلعَالَمِينَ وَنُورًا، وَمَلأَ بِمَولِدِهِ الْقُلُوبَ سُرُورًا
verses.tr: Wa jaʿalahu raḥmatan lil-ʿālamīna wa nūran, wa malaʾa bi-mawlidihil-qulūba surūrā
verses.en: He made him a mercy to all the worlds and a light, and filled hearts with joy through his birth.

verses.ar: اللّٰهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ وَبَارِكْ عَلَيْهِ وَعَلٰى آلِهْ
verses.tr: Allāhumma ṣalli wa sallim wa bārik ʿalayhi wa ʿalā ālih
verses.en: O Allah, bless him, grant him peace, and pour Your blessings upon him and his family.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Gelin Ey Aşıklar — Come, O Lovers
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). Each line is followed by the invocation “Hû Mevlam Hû Hû.”

verses.ar:
Gelin ey aşıklar gelin · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Bu menzil uzağa benzer · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: Come, O lovers, come — Hû, my Lord, Hû Hû; this way-station seems far away — Hû, my Lord, Hû Hû.

verses.ar:
Nazar kıldım şu dünyaya · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Kurulmuş tuzağa benzer · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: I gazed upon this world — it seems like a snare that has been set.

verses.ar:
Bir pirin eteğin tuttum · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Ona beli deyip gittim · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: I took hold of a master's hem; I gave him my pledge and went on my way.

verses.ar:
Nice yüzbin günah ettim · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Herbiri bir dağa benzer · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: How many hundred-thousand sins I have committed — each one seems like a mountain.

verses.ar:
Ağla aşık Yunus ağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Sen özünü Hakk'a bağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: Weep, lover Yunus, weep; bind your very self to the Truth (God).

verses.ar:
Ağlar isen kendine ağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Elden vefa yoğa benzer · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: If you weep, weep for yourself — loyalty from others seems not to exist.

verses.ar:
Ağla aşık Yunus ağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Sen özünü Hakk'a bağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: Weep, lover Yunus, weep; bind your very self to the Truth (God).

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Güzel Aşık Cevrimizi — Fair Lover, Our Trial

verses.ar:
Güzel aşık cevrimizi
Çekemezsin demedim mi
Bu bir rıza lokmasıdır
Yiyemezsin demedim mi
verses.en: Fair lover, did I not tell you that you could not bear the trial we bring? This is a morsel of [divine] contentment — did I not tell you that you could not swallow it?

verses.ar:
Yemeyenler kalır naçar
Gözlerinden kanlar saçar
Bu bir demdir gelir geçer
Duyamazsın demedim mi
verses.en: Those who do not eat it are left helpless, scattering tears of blood from their eyes. This is a moment that comes and passes — did I not tell you that you could not perceive it?

verses.ar:
Bu dervişlik bir dilektir
Bilene büyük devlettir
Yensiz yakasız gömlektir
Giyemezsin demedim mi
verses.en: This dervishhood is a calling — to the one who knows it, a great fortune. It is a shirt with no sleeves and no collar — did I not tell you that you could not wear it?

verses.ar:
Çıkalım meydan yerine
Erelim Ali sırrına
Can ü başı Hak yoluna
Koyamazsın demedim mi
verses.en: Let us step out into the gathering-place and reach the secret of Ali; your life and your head upon the path of the Truth — did I not tell you that you could not lay them down?

verses.ar:
Aşıklar kara bahtı olur
Hakk'ın katında kutlu olur
Muhabbet baldan tatlı olur
Yiyemezsin demedim mi
verses.en: Lovers are of dark fortune, yet blessed in the presence of the Truth. Love is sweeter than honey — did I not tell you that you could not taste it?

verses.ar:
Pir Sultan Abdal Şahımız
Hakk'a ulaşır rahımız
On İki İmam katarımız
Uyamazsın demedim mi
verses.en: Pir Sultan Abdal is our Shah; our path reaches the Truth. The Twelve Imams are our caravan — did I not tell you that you could not keep pace with it?

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Yemen İllerinde Veysel Karani — Veysel Karani in the Lands of Yemen
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.), in praise of Uways al-Qaranī, the Prophet's ﷺ devoted follower from Yemen.

verses.ar:
Hakk'ın Habibi'nin sevgili dostu
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: The beloved friend of the Beloved of the Truth — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

verses.ar:
Söylemez yalanı, yemez haramı
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: He tells no lie and eats nothing forbidden — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

verses.ar:
Seherde kalkuben yola giderdi
Hakk'ın binbir ismin zikir ederdi
Allah Allah deyu deve güderdi
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: He would rise at dawn and set out on his way, calling upon the thousand-and-one names of the Truth; saying 'Allah, Allah' he would tend his camels — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

verses.ar:
Elinde asası hurma dalından
Eğninde hırkası deve yününden
Asla hata gelmez onun dilinden
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: In his hand a staff of palm-branch, on his shoulders a cloak of camel's wool; never does a wrong word come from his tongue — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

verses.ar:
Aşık Yunus eydür ben de varaydım
Ol mübarek hub cemalin göreydim
Ayağın tozuna yüzler süreydim
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: Yunus the lover says: would that I too could go, that I might behold that blessed, lovely face, and press my face into the dust of his feet — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Şu Cennetin İrmakları — The Rivers of Paradise
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). Each couplet closes with the refrain “Allah deyu deyu” — “saying: Allah, Allah.”

verses.ar:
Şol cennetin ırmakları akar Allah deyu deyu
Çıkmış İslam bülbülleri öter Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: The rivers of that Paradise flow on, saying: Allah, Allah; the nightingales of Islam have risen and sing, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Salınır tûba dalları Kur'an okur hem dilleri
Cennet bağının gülleri kokar Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: The branches of the Tuba tree sway, and their tongues recite the Qur'an; the roses of the garden of Paradise give off their scent, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Kimi yiyip kimi içer hep melekler rahmet saçar
İdris nebî hûlle biçer biçer Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Some eat and some drink, and everywhere the angels scatter mercy; the prophet Idris cuts out robes of honour, cutting, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Altındandır direkleri gümüştendir yaprakları
Uzandıkça budakları biter Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Its pillars are of gold, its leaves are of silver; as its branches stretch out they bud and grow, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Aydan arıdır yüzleri misk-i amberdir sözleri
Cennette Huri kızları gezer Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Their faces are purer than the moon, their words are musk and amber; the maidens of Paradise stroll about, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Hakka aşık olan kişi akar gözlerinin yaşı
Pür nûr olur içi dışı söyler Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: The one who loves the Truth — the tears stream from their eyes; their inward and outward being becomes full of light, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Ne dilersen Hak'tan dile kılavuzla gir bu yola
Bülbül aşık olmuş güle öter Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Whatever you wish, ask it of the Truth; enter this path with a guide; the nightingale has fallen in love with the rose and sings, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Açıldı gökler kapısı rahmetle doldu hepisi
Sekiz cennetin kapısı açar Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: The gate of the heavens has opened, and all of them are filled with mercy; the gates of the eight Paradises open, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Rıdvan'durur kapı açan İdris'durur hûlle biçen
Kevser şarabını içen kanar Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: It is Ridwan who opens the gate, it is Idris who cuts the robes of honour; the one who drinks the wine of Kawthar is quenched, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Miskin Yunus var yârına koma bugünü yarına
Yarın Hakkın divanına varam Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Poor Yunus, go to your Beloved; do not put off today until tomorrow; tomorrow I shall come before the court of the Truth, saying: Allah, Allah.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Sordum Sarı Çiçeğe — I Asked the Yellow Flower
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). A dialogue between the dervish and a fading yellow flower; each verse closes on the refrain of tawḥīd.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Annen baban var mıdır?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Annem babam topraktır
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: have you a mother and father? The flower said, 'Dervish father, my mother and father are the earth.' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Sen kimin ümmetisin?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Muhammed ümmetiyim
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: whose community are you of? The flower said, 'Dervish father, I am of Muhammad's community.' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Evlat kardeş var mıdır?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Evlat kardeş yapraktır
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: have you children and siblings? The flower said, 'Dervish father, my children and siblings are the leaves.' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Niçin benzin sarıdır?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Ölüm bize yakındır
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: why is your face so pale? The flower said, 'Dervish father, death is near to us.' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Sen beni bilir misin?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Sen Yunus değil misin?
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: do you know me? The flower said, 'Dervish father, are you not Yunus?' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Dolap Niçin İnilersin — Dertli Dolap (The Sorrowful Waterwheel)
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). The water-wheel speaks: the felled tree that groans in longing for its Lord.

verses.ar:
Dolap niçin inilersin
Derdim vardır inilerim
Ben Mevlâ'ya âşık oldum
Anın için inilerim
verses.en: O waterwheel, why do you groan? I have a sorrow, so I groan. I have fallen in love with my Lord; for His sake I groan.

verses.ar:
Benim adım dertli dolap
Suyum akar yalap yalap
Böyle emreylemiş Çalap
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: My name is the sorrowful wheel; my water flows glinting and gleaming. So has God ordained; I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Beni bir dağda buldular
Kolum kanadım yoldular
Dolaba lâyık gördüler
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: They found me upon a mountain; they tore away my arms and wings; they deemed me fit to be a wheel. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Ben bir dağın ağacıyım
Ne tatlıyım ne acıyım
Ben Mevlâ'ya duacıyım
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: I am a tree of the mountain; I am neither sweet nor bitter. I am one who prays to my Lord. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Dağdan kestiler hezenim
Bozuldu türlü düzenim
Ben bir usanmaz ozanım
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: They cut my great beams from the mountain; all my order was undone. I am a minstrel who never tires. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Şu dülgerler beni yondu
Her azam yerine kondu
Bu iniltim Hak'tan geldi
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: These carpenters carved me; each of my limbs was set in its place. This groaning of mine came from the Truth. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Suyum alçaktan çekerim
Dönüp yükseğe dökerim
Görün ben neler çekerim
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: I draw my water from below, and turning, pour it out on high. See what I endure! I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Yunus burda gelen gülmez
Kişi muradına ermez
Bu fânide kimse kalmaz
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: Yunus: none who comes here laughs; no one attains their heart's desire; no one remains in this passing world. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: İlim İlim Bilmektir — Knowledge Is to Know
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). True knowledge is self-knowledge and knowing God — worth more than a thousand pilgrimages.

verses.ar:
İlim ilim bilmektir
İlim kendin bilmektir
Sen kendini bilmezsin
Ya nice okumaktır
verses.en: Knowledge is to know knowledge; knowledge is to know your own self. If you do not know yourself, then what is all this reading for?

verses.ar:
Okumaktan mana ne
Kişi Hakk'ı bilmektir
Çün okudun bilmezsin
Ha bir kuru emektir
verses.en: What is the meaning of reading? It is for one to know the Truth. If you have read yet still do not know, it is but dry, empty toil.

verses.ar:
Okudum bildim deme
Çok tâat kıldım deme
Eğer Hak bilmez isen
Abes yere yelmektir
verses.en: Do not say 'I have read and I know'; do not say 'I have worshipped much.' If you do not know the Truth, it is only running about in vain.

verses.ar:
Dört kitabın mânâsı
Bellidir bir elifte
Sen elifi bilmezsin
Bu nice okumaktır
verses.en: The meaning of the four Books is made plain in a single Alif. You do not know even the Alif — so what is all this reading?

verses.ar:
Yunus Emre der hoca
Gerekse bin var hacca
Hepisinden iyice
Bir gönüle girmektir
verses.en: Yunus Emre says: O teacher, though you go a thousand times to the Hajj — better than all of it is to enter and win a single heart.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Adı Güzel Kendi Güzel Muhammed — Beautiful of Name, Beautiful of Self
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: A beloved naʿt attributed to Yunus Emre (13th c.), in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.

verses.ar:
Canım kurban olsun senin yoluna
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
Şefâat eyle bu kemter kuluna
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: May my life be a sacrifice on your path — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self. Intercede for this lowly servant — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

verses.ar:
Mü'min olanların çoktur cefâsı
Ahirette olur zevk ü sefâsı
On sekiz bin âlemin Mustafâ'sı
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: Those who believe bear much hardship; their joy and ease will come in the Hereafter. The Chosen One of the eighteen thousand worlds — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

verses.ar:
Yedi kat gökleri seyrân eyleyen
Kürsü'nün üstünde cevlân eyleyen
Mi'racda ümmetini dileyen
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: He who journeyed through the seven heavens, who moved above the Divine Footstool, who on the Ascension pleaded for his community — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

verses.ar:
Ol çâryâr anın gökçek yâridir
Anı seven günahlardan beridir
On sekiz bin âlemin serveridir
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: The four rightly-guided companions are his fair friends; whoever loves him is freed of sins. He is the master of the eighteen thousand worlds — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

verses.ar:
Âşık Yunus neyler iki cihânı sensiz
Sen hak Peygambersin şeksiz şüphesiz
Sana uymayanlar gider imansız
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: What would Yunus the lover do with both worlds without you? You are the true Prophet, beyond doubt or question. Those who do not follow you depart without faith — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Derman Arardım Derdime — I Sought a Cure for My Ailment
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: By Niyazi Mısrî (17th c.). A classic of Sufi realization: the cure, the proof, and the Beloved were within all along.

verses.ar:
Derman arardım derdime
Derdim bana derman imiş
Bürhan sorardım aslıma
Aslım bana bürhan imiş
verses.en: I sought a cure for my ailment — my ailment itself was my cure. I sought a proof of my origin — my origin itself was my proof.

verses.ar:
Sağ u solum gözler idim
Dost yüzünü görsem deyu
Ben taşrada arar idim
Ol can içinde can imiş
verses.en: I searched to my right and left, longing to see the Friend's face; I was seeking outside, yet He was the very soul within the soul.

verses.ar:
Öyle sanırdım ayriyem
Dost gayridir ben gayriyem
Benden görüp işiteni
Bildim ki ol cânân imiş
verses.en: I used to think I was apart — that the Friend was other and I was other; then I knew that the One who sees and hears through me is the Beloved.

verses.ar:
Savm u salât u hac ile
Sanma biter zâhid işin
İnsan-ı kâmil olmaya
Lâzım olan irfan imiş
verses.en: Do not imagine, O ascetic, that your work is finished with fasting, prayer, and pilgrimage; what is needed to become a perfected human being is inner gnosis.

verses.ar:
Mürşid gerektir bildire
Hakk'ı sana Hakka'l-yakîn
Mürşidi olmayanların
Bildikleri gümân imiş
verses.en: A guide is needed to make you know the Truth with the certainty of direct knowledge; what those without a guide know is mere conjecture.

verses.ar:
Anla hemen bir sözdürür
Yokuş değildir düzdürür
Âlem kamu bir yüzdürür
Gören anı hayran imiş
verses.en: Understand at once: it is a single word, no steep climb but level ground; all the world is one single face — whoever sees it is lost in wonder.

verses.ar:
İşit Niyazi'nin sözün
Bir nesne örtmez Hak yüzün
Hak'tan ayan bir nesne yok
Gözsüzlere pinhan imiş
verses.en: Hear the word of Niyazi: nothing veils the face of the Truth; nothing is more manifest than the Truth — yet to the sightless it stays hidden.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Dağlar İle Taşlar İle — Let Me Call Upon You, My Lord
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). With all of creation — mountains, birds, prophets — the poet calls upon his Lord.

verses.ar:
Dağlar ile taşlar ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
Seherlerde kuşlar ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With the mountains and the stones, let me call upon You, my Lord; with the birds at daybreak, let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Sular dibinde mâhi ile
Sahralarda âhu ile
Abdal olup yâhu ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With the fish in the depths of the waters, with the gazelle upon the open plains, becoming a wandering dervish crying 'Yā Hū' — let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Gökyüzünde İsa ile
Tur dağında Musa ile
Elimdeki asâ ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With Jesus in the heavens, with Moses on Mount Tur, with the staff in my hand — let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Derdi öküş Eyyub ile
Gözü yaşlı Yakub ile
Ol Muhammed mahbub ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With sorely-afflicted Job, with tearful-eyed Jacob, with Muhammad the beloved — let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Hamd ü şükrullah ile
Vasf-ı Kulhüvallah ile
Dâima zikrullah ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With praise and thanks to Allah, with the words 'Say: He is Allah,' always with the remembrance of Allah — let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Bilmişim dünya hâlini
Terk ettim kıyl ü kâlini
Baş açık ayak yalını
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: I have come to know the ways of this world; I have left its idle talk behind. Bare-headed and barefoot, let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Yunus okur diller ile
Ol kumru bülbüller ile
Hakk'ı seven kullar ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: Yunus recites with many tongues, with the doves and the nightingales, with the servants who love the Truth — let me call upon You, my Lord.

ILAHI_CHAPTERS.titleEnglish: Arayı Arayı Bulsam İzini — O Muhammad, My Soul Longs for You
ILAHI_CHAPTERS.note: A beloved naʿt in the tradition of Yunus Emre (13th c.), yearning for the Prophet ﷺ and his city.

verses.ar:
Arayı arayı bulsam izini
İzinin tozuna sürsem yüzümü
Hak nasip eylese görsem yüzünü
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: If only, searching and searching, I could find his track and press my face into the dust of his footprints; if God would grant that I might see his face — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.

verses.ar:
Bir mübarek sefer olsa da gitsem
Kâbe yollarında kumlara batsam
Hûb cemâlin bir kez düşte seyretsem
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: If only there were a blessed journey and I could go, sinking into the sands on the roads to the Kaaba; if I could gaze upon your lovely face just once, even in a dream — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.

verses.ar:
Zerrece kalmadı kalbimde hile
Sıtk ile girmişim ben hak yola
Ebû Bekir, Ömer, Osman'da bile
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: Not a speck of guile remains in my heart; I have entered the true path in sincerity — alongside Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.

verses.ar:
Ali ile Hasan Hüseyin anda
Sevgisi gönülde muhabbeti canda
Yarın mahşer günü ulu divanda
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: With Ali, and with Hasan and Husayn there — their love in the heart, their affection in the soul — tomorrow on the Day of Gathering, in the great assembly — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.

verses.ar:
Arafat dağıdır bizim dağımız
Anda kabul olur bizim duamız
Medine'de yatar Peygamberimiz
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: Mount Arafat is our mountain; there our prayers are answered; in Medina rests our Prophet — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.
